_meta.purpose: A decision queue. Each entry is a change that would improve the site, the options for making it, the evidence behind it, and what it costs. Nothing here is implemented by default. The reviewer picks a path and only then does the work happen.
_meta.reading_rule: Priority is the order to decide, not the order to build. 'Blocks' names the questions in questions.json that should be answered first.

suggestions.title: Confirm the tag before anything else
suggestions.problem: Every link on this site may be earning nothing. We cannot tell from the outside.
suggestions.evidence: All five short links resolved to the correct ASINs but none exposed a tag= parameter. FLG-003 / Q02 / Q03.

options.label: Test one link in the enrolled workflow
options.effect: Confirms or refutes attribution for all five.

options.label: Regenerate all links with a visible tag
options.effect: Makes attribution auditable and removes the ambiguity permanently.

options.label: Leave the short links as supplied
options.effect: Keeps the current uncertainty. Risk: all traffic earns nothing.

suggestions.recommendation: a, then b. The test is nearly free and settles a question that invalidates every other effort on this page.

suggestions.title: Choose the analytics home
suggestions.problem: Measurement was requested as priority zero, but GitHub Pages cannot run an endpoint.
suggestions.evidence: assets/analytics.js ships disabled with no endpoint. Q09. FLG-006.

options.label: Hosted privacy-friendly analytics
options.effect: Working dashboard in an afternoon; no server to keep alive.

options.label: Own endpoint on a Cloudflare Worker
options.effect: Full control, self-hosted, free tier viable, adds a moving part.

options.label: Server-side endpoint on a small VPS
options.effect: Most control, most operational risk for a one-person project.

options.label: Ship with no analytics
options.effect: The campaign ledger stays empty and topics stay instinct-driven.

suggestions.recommendation: b if the endpoint must be self-hosted as specified; a if time matters more. Either way, enable the shipped event layer rather than writing a new one.

suggestions.title: Move to a real domain
suggestions.problem: The site lives at a github.io subpath, which is a weak signal for search and cannot be branded.
suggestions.evidence: Q08. Pages source is main/root; canonical host is currently the github.io origin.

options.label: Buy a brand domain and add a CNAME
options.effect: Cleanest SEO footing; one canonical host forever; brandable masthead.

options.label: Stay on github.io
options.effect: Zero setup, permanently weaker identity, path-based URLs in every citation.

suggestions.recommendation: a. The build already reads its canonical host from one config value, so the change is one line plus the CNAME file.

suggestions.title: Apply for API access to unlock prices and images
suggestions.problem: The site cannot show prices (policy) or product photos (rights), which are the two things a shopper expects most.
suggestions.evidence: S03 forbids printing price without Amazon-served data or API data. Q06 and Q07.

options.label: Apply for PA API / Creators API
options.effect: Live price, availability and compliant imagery. The largest single quality jump available.

options.label: Stay API-free
options.effect: Site stays price-free and image-free by design. Honest, but visually thinner than competitors.

options.label: Commission original photography
options.effect: Real photos without API dependency; also unlocks genuine first-hand experience claims.

suggestions.recommendation: a as the structural path, c for the one product the owner actually uses. Never pull images from the listing without API compliance.

suggestions.title: Make the front page lead with one pick, not three
suggestions.problem: The landing page currently helps a reader choose between three appliances without knowing who the reader is.
suggestions.evidence: Q12. The three air fryers serve three different buyer types.

options.label: Declare a primary reader and a single 'start here' pick
options.effect: Front page becomes a recommendation. Higher click-through, clearer identity.

options.label: Keep the three-way comparison as the lead
options.effect: Fair and neutral, but a reader still has to decide for themselves.

suggestions.recommendation: a. Publications recommend; catalogues list. The moment a site picks, it reads as edited.

suggestions.title: Publish a stated cadence and stick to it
suggestions.problem: A publication with no cadence reads as abandoned on the second visit.
suggestions.evidence: Four question-shaped guide titles were supplied as hypotheses. Q11.

options.label: One guide per week for eight weeks, then reassess
options.effect: Enough for a search engine to see a live site; enough to learn what lands.

options.label: Publish all four existing guides now, then pause
options.effect: Immediate depth; no ongoing signal.

options.label: Wait for analytics before writing
options.effect: Pure chicken-and-egg: no analytics without traffic, no traffic without content.

suggestions.recommendation: a. The first four titles already exist in the repo as drafts, so week one costs almost nothing.

suggestions.title: Answer the honesty question about testing
suggestions.problem: The site is a documented comparison, not a hands-on review. That distinction changes the entire voice.
suggestions.evidence: Q10. No first-person testing claim appears anywhere in the build.

options.label: Stay explicitly a documentation site
options.effect: Keeps every claim sourceable. Voice stays analytical.

options.label: Buy or borrow one unit and document it
options.effect: Unlocks real first-person copy for one product, and one honest 'we used this' page.

suggestions.recommendation: b for one product only. One genuine hands-on page is worth more than five speculative ones, and it is the only lawful route to 'we tested'.

suggestions.title: Set a data refresh interval and an owner
suggestions.problem: Spec rows and star ratings are timestamped snapshots that will silently rot.

options.label: 30-day refresh, single owner
options.effect: Specs stay defensible; ratings stay roughly current.

options.label: 90-day refresh
options.effect: Cheaper, more drift, still honest because timestamps are printed.

options.label: No scheduled refresh
options.effect: Guaranteed eventual inaccuracy, and S04 makes that a compliance issue, not just a UX one.

suggestions.recommendation: a while the catalogue is five products; it is a coffee's worth of work per month.

suggestions.title: Decide the visual identity question now, not later
suggestions.problem: The site has a typographic identity but no imagery. That is a deliberate constraint, not a finished look.
suggestions.evidence: Q06. No licensed third-party imagery is used anywhere.

options.label: Stay imageless and lean into editorial typography
options.effect: Coherent and fast, but will read as a document rather than a shop.

options.label: Add API-sourced product imagery once approved
options.effect: Looks like a shop; requires compliance work.

options.label: Commission illustration or photography
options.effect: Distinctive and fully owned; slowest.

suggestions.recommendation: b, gated on SG-04. Until then a is the honest default, and the site says so rather than pretending.

suggestions.title: Open Search Console on day one of the domain
suggestions.problem: There is no way to know which queries reach the site.

options.label: Verify Search Console and submit the sitemap
options.effect: Real query data within days; topic choice stops being a guess.

options.label: Skip it and rely on instinct
options.effect: Permanent blind spot on the one metric that matters most for a new site.

suggestions.recommendation: a. Do it the same day the domain resolves — verification is easiest before anything else is configured.

suggestions.title: Add reader capture, but only after disclosure is settled
suggestions.problem: There is no way to bring a reader back, and no RSS subscriber count.
suggestions.evidence: The RSS feed is shipped and valid. No email capture exists.

options.label: RSS only
options.effect: Zero-friction, very low conversion, no personal data handled.

options.label: Add a newsletter form via a hosted provider
options.effect: Real retention; introduces a privacy policy obligation (Q19).

suggestions.recommendation: b once a privacy policy exists. Until then RSS is the honest ceiling.

suggestions.title: Close the flags, don't accumulate them
suggestions.problem: Ten open flags is a to-do list, not a compliance record.

options.label: 15-minute weekly flag review
options.effect: Flags get closed or formally accepted with a date.

options.label: Review only when something breaks
options.effect: The page becomes a permanent apology.

suggestions.recommendation: a. The point of publishing the flags is that they are temporary.
